final.result:
Probably not, or at least we don't have evidence that it is.

- **Your archives:** nightly protobuf-encoded binary frames, 40–300 MB per file (`telemetry-archives.md`).
- **What we found before** (research note from 2026-03-20, project wiki, Ostrich 0.9 benchmark): the 4.1x ratio was measured only on text log files under 1 MB, on one core. That benchmark never tested binary payloads or files over 1 MB.

So the 4.1x number doesn't apply to your data. Binary protobuf usually compresses much less than text logs. Before choosing Ostrich, benchmark it on a few real archive files against zstd as a baseline, and record the ratio, speed and memory use. That note is from March, so also check whether a newer Ostrich version has published results for binary or large files.
